passages.p1: Read the email from Leo to his friend. Choose the correct word for each gap. The first one is done for you. Dear Max, This morning I woke up and saw the first [[1]]. Everything outside was white and very [[2]]. My brother and I made a big [[3]]. We had a fun [[4]] with soft snowballs. My fingers got really [[5]] outside. Then we drank hot [[6]] in the kitchen.
passages.p2: Put the sentences in the correct order. The first sentence is fixed.
passages.p3:
A. As cities grow more crowded and polluted, the humble bicycle is enjoying a remarkable revival. Once seen by many as a child's toy or a poor person's transport, it is now celebrated as a clever solution to modern problems. Planners praise it as cheap, clean and space-efficient all at once. A simple machine invented long ago suddenly looks strikingly modern.

B. The advantages of cycling for the individual are hard to ignore. It costs little to buy and almost nothing to run, sparing riders the expense of fuel and parking. Regular cycling also keeps people fit, turning the daily commute into a dose of exercise. For short journeys in busy areas, a bike is often faster than a car stuck in traffic.

C. The benefits ripple outwards to the city as a whole. Every person who switches from a car to a bicycle means one less vehicle clogging the roads and polluting the air. Bicycles take up little space, so more of them can move and park in the same area. The result is quieter streets and cleaner skies for everyone.

D. Yet many would-be cyclists are held back by a single powerful fear. Sharing busy roads with fast-moving traffic feels dangerous, and the risk is not merely imagined. Without protection, even confident riders can be intimidated by lorries and impatient drivers. Until streets feel safe, the bicycle's potential will remain only partly realised.

E. The cities that have succeeded share one clear lesson. Where authorities build separated cycle lanes and calm traffic, cycling rates soar within a few years. Good infrastructure signals that bikes belong on the road and reassures nervous beginners. Investment in safety, it turns out, is the surest way to fill the lanes.

F. Technology is widening the appeal of two wheels still further. Electric bicycles flatten hills and shrink long distances, bringing cycling within reach of older or less fit riders. Shared bike schemes let people grab a machine for a single trip without owning one at all. These innovations are quietly broadening who can take part.

G. Looking ahead, the bicycle seems set to play an ever larger role in how we move. As concerns about health, cost and the climate mount, its simple efficiency only grows more attractive. Cities that embrace it are likely to become more pleasant places to live. The future of urban transport may, in part, run on pedal power.

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

He _____ born in 1990.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. "1990" = mốc thời gian quá khứ cụ thể
2. "be born" dạng bị động → was/were born
3. Đáp án: {was} — was born + năm
[/tuduy]
[td]Anh ấy sinh năm 1990.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

I have _____ been to Japan.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. Ngữ cảnh: chưa từng đến → phủ định kinh nghiệm
2. "never" đặt giữa have và V3 (been)
3. Đáp án: {never} — have never been to
[/tuduy]
[td]Tôi chưa bao giờ đến Nhật Bản.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

We _____ study harder for the next exam.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. Ngữ cảnh: cần nỗ lực hơn cho kỳ thi → nghĩa vụ/bắt buộc
2. "must" = phải (bắt buộc, cần thiết)
3. Đáp án: {must} — bắt buộc
[/tuduy]
[td]Chúng ta phải học chăm hơn cho kỳ thi tới.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

The match _____ at three o'clock tomorrow.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. Lịch trình/thời gian biểu cố định → dùng hiện tại đơn
2. Dù nói về tương lai, lịch chính thức dùng present simple
3. Đáp án: {starts} — present simple cho lịch trình
[/tuduy]
[td]Trận đấu bắt đầu lúc ba giờ ngày mai.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

She left her keys _____ the table.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. Chìa khóa nằm trên bề mặt bàn → giới từ chỉ vị trí bề mặt
2. "on" = trên bề mặt; "in" = bên trong; "at" = tại (điểm)
3. Đáp án: {on} — on the table
[/tuduy]
[td]Cô ấy để chìa khóa trên bàn.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

This is the _____ interesting book I've ever read.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. "I've ever read" → so sánh nhất
2. "interesting" nhiều âm tiết → the most + adj
3. Đáp án: {most} — the most interesting
[/tuduy]
[td]Đây là cuốn sách thú vị nhất mà tôi từng đọc.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

He hasn't done his homework _____.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. Câu phủ định hiện tại hoàn thành → dùng "yet" (chưa)
2. "already" cho câu khẳng định; "yet" cho câu phủ định/nghi vấn
3. Đáp án: {yet} — hasn't… yet
[/tuduy]
[td]Anh ấy chưa làm bài tập về nhà.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

There aren't _____ eggs in the fridge.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. "eggs" là danh từ đếm được số nhiều
2. Danh từ đếm được + câu phủ định → dùng "many"
3. Đáp án: {many} — many + countable (phủ định)
[/tuduy]
[td]Không có nhiều trứng trong tủ lạnh.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

By the time we got there, the film _____.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. "got" = quá khứ đơn → hành động bắt đầu phim xảy ra TRƯỚC đó
2. Hành động trước quá khứ → quá khứ hoàn thành
3. Đáp án: {had started} — past perfect
[/tuduy]
[td]Khi chúng tôi đến nơi, phim đã bắt đầu rồi.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

If it rains tomorrow, we _____ stay at home.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. "If + hiện tại đơn" → câu điều kiện loại 1 (có thể xảy ra)
2. Mệnh đề chính: will + V nguyên mẫu
3. Đáp án: {will} — first conditional
[/tuduy]
[td]Nếu ngày mai trời mưa, chúng ta sẽ ở nhà.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

She _____ play the piano very well.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. "play very well" → diễn tả khả năng
2. "can" = có khả năng; "must" = phải; "should" = nên
3. Đáp án: {can} — khả năng
[/tuduy]
[td]Cô ấy chơi piano rất giỏi.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

They _____ to the cinema last weekend.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. "last weekend" → thời gian xác định trong quá khứ
2. Thời gian xác định → quá khứ đơn (không dùng hiện tại hoàn thành)
3. Đáp án: {went} — past simple
[/tuduy]
[td]Họ đã đi xem phim cuối tuần trước.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

You _____ turn off your phone in the cinema.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. Rạp chiếu phim → quy định bắt buộc tắt điện thoại
2. "must" = bắt buộc; "can" = có thể; "might" = có lẽ
3. Đáp án: {must} — bắt buộc
[/tuduy]
[td]Bạn phải tắt điện thoại trong rạp phim.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

She _____ be at home now. Her car is in the drive.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. "Her car is in the drive" → bằng chứng rõ ràng
2. Suy luận chắc chắn từ bằng chứng → must
3. Đáp án: {must} — suy luận chắc chắn
[/tuduy]
[td]Cô ấy chắc hẳn đang ở nhà. Xe cô ấy đỗ ở lối vào.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

You _____ be tired after such a long journey.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. "such a long journey" → suy luận chắc chắn từ bằng chứng
2. "must" = chắc hẳn (suy luận logic)
3. Đáp án: {must} — suy luận chắc chắn
[/tuduy]
[td]Bạn chắc hẳn mệt sau chuyến đi dài như vậy.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

He _____ speak French when he was five.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. "when he was five" → khả năng trong quá khứ
2. "could" = dạng quá khứ của "can"
3. Đáp án: {could} — khả năng quá khứ
[/tuduy]
[td]Anh ấy biết nói tiếng Pháp khi mới năm tuổi.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

You _____ drive so fast. It’s dangerous.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. "It’s dangerous" → cảnh báo KHÔNG ĐƯỢC làm
2. "mustn't" = cấm; "don't have to" = không cần
3. Đáp án: {mustn't} — cấm đoán
[/tuduy]
[td]Bạn không được lái xe nhanh như vậy. Nguy hiểm lắm.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

You _____ eat more vegetables. They're good for you.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. "They're good for you" → lời khuyên
2. "should" = nên (lời khuyên); "must" = phải (bắt buộc)
3. Đáp án: {should} — lời khuyên
[/tuduy]
[td]Bạn nên ăn nhiều rau hơn. Rau tốt cho sức khỏe.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

You _____ come if you don’t want to. It’s your choice.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. "It’s your choice" → KHÔNG bắt buộc (tùy bạn)
2. "don't have to" = không cần/không bắt buộc
3. Đáp án: {don't have to} — không bắt buộc
[/tuduy]
[td]Bạn không cần phải đến nếu không muốn. Tùy bạn.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

I wish I _____ taller.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. "I wish" + mong muốn trái ngược hiện tại → dùng thì quá khứ đơn
2. Với "be": I wish I were (không dùng "was" trong văn chuẩn)
3. Đáp án: {were} — wish + were
[/tuduy]
[td]Ước gì tôi cao hơn.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

_____ I open the window? It's hot in here.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. Đề nghị giúp hoặc hỏi ý kiến → "Shall I…?"
2. "Must" = bắt buộc; "Would" dùng cho yêu cầu lịch sự
3. Đáp án: {Shall} — đề nghị: Shall I…?
[/tuduy]
[td]Để tôi mở cửa sổ nhé? Nóng quá.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

I _____ like a cup of coffee, please.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. Yêu cầu lịch sự khi gọi đồ → "I would like…"
2. "would like" = muốn (lịch sự hơn "want")
3. Đáp án: {would} — I would like…
[/tuduy]
[td]Tôi muốn một tách cà phê, làm ơn.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

You _____ park here. It's not allowed.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. "It's not allowed" → CẤM, không được phép
2. "mustn't" = cấm; "don't have to" = không cần; "shouldn't" = không nên
3. Đáp án: {mustn't} — cấm đoán
[/tuduy]
[td]Bạn không được đỗ xe ở đây. Không được phép.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

That _____ Marcus at the door; he said he might drop by sometime this evening to return the book.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. Nhận diện động từ "_____ Marcus" cần chia theo thì tương lai. 
2. Quy tắc thì tương lai đơn sử dụng "will" + động từ nguyên thể. 
3. Đáp án: {will be} — thì tương lai đơn dùng "will" để diễn tả hành động tương lai. 
[/tuduy]
[td]"Đó sẽ là Marcus ở cửa; anh ấy nói rằng có thể sẽ ghé qua tối nay để trả sách." [/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

There's no point waiting any longer; he _____ have forgotten about the appointment entirely.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. Nhận diện "he _____ have forgotten" là cấu trúc diễn tả khả năng.
2. "may" được dùng để chỉ khả năng xảy ra trong hiện tại.
3. Đáp án: {may} — "may" diễn tả khả năng trong hiện tại.
[/tuduy]
[td]Không có lý do gì để chờ đợi lâu hơn; có thể anh ấy đã quên hoàn toàn cuộc hẹn. [/td]

questions.content:
Writing — Part 3 - Three responses

Omar: Hi! My neighbour plays rock music, and I like rock too, but I don't want to hear it every day. Can you give me some advice?
questions.sampleAnswer: I understand your problem. I think you should talk to your neighbour politely and explain your feelings. You could agree on quiet hours together. If that does not work, using headphones at home might help you relax.

questions.content:
Writing — Part 3 - Three responses

Hana: My father doesn't enjoy listening to music, though I loved it when I was young. Why does music change from generation to generation?
questions.sampleAnswer: Music changes because every generation has different experiences and feelings. Young people often enjoy new sounds and technology, while older people prefer familiar songs. This natural difference explains why our musical tastes keep changing over time.

questions.content:
Writing — Part 3 - Three responses

Tariq: Do you agree that music is important in culture?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I strongly agree that music is important in culture. It expresses our traditions, emotions, and history through songs. For example, at festivals in my country, traditional music brings families together and keeps old customs alive.

questions.content:
Writing — Part 4 - Informal and formal emails

Write an email to your friend. Write about your feelings and what ideas you have. Write about 50 words. Recommended time: 10 minutes.
questions.sampleAnswer:
Hi Nora!
Our book circle gets to help redesign part of the city library — how exciting! Most people think libraries are boring, so I'd love to see a cosy reading lounge with bean bags, a kids' storytelling corner, and maybe even a little café. That would make such a difference!
Can't wait to share ideas,
Finn

questions.content:
Writing — Part 4 - Informal and formal emails

Write an email to the design team. Write about your suggestions and explain how they would attract different age groups. Write 120–150 words. Recommended time: 20 minutes.
questions.sampleAnswer:
Dear Design Team,
I am writing to share my suggestions for the new library section. I believe that with the right design, we can transform the space into somewhere people of all ages genuinely want to spend time.
For younger visitors, I suggest a dedicated children's area with colourful seating, interactive reading stations, and a weekly storytelling hour. This would encourage parents to bring their children and help build reading habits from an early age.
For adult and older readers, a quiet reading lounge with comfortable armchairs, good lighting, and access to both physical books and digital resources would create a welcoming atmosphere. A small café corner would also make the library feel more social and inviting.
Finally, hosting regular events such as author talks, book swaps, and creative writing workshops would give people a reason to visit regularly.
I hope these ideas prove useful.
Yours sincerely,
Sophia Walters

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 2 - Describe a picture

Describe the picture.
questions.sampleAnswer: I see a group of people studying together. They are sitting around a table with books and laptops. They are reading and discussing. They look focused and serious about their study.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 2 - Describe a picture

Do you prefer studying alone or in a group? Why?
questions.sampleAnswer: I prefer studying in a group because we can help each other. When I don't understand something, my friends explain it to me. But sometimes I study alone when I need to concentrate.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 2 - Describe a picture

What are the benefits of studying together?
questions.sampleAnswer: Studying together has many benefits. You can share ideas and learn from each other. If you don't understand a lesson, friends can help. It is also more motivating because you don't feel lazy when others are studying.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 3 - Compare two pictures

Describe the two pictures.
questions.sampleAnswer: In the first picture, I see children visiting a garden with their teacher. They are looking at plants and flowers outside. They look happy and curious. It is a sunny day. In the second picture, I see children in a classroom. They are raising their hands to answer the teacher's questions. They sit at desks. The classroom is bright and tidy.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 3 - Compare two pictures

What are the benefits of learning outdoors and in a classroom?
questions.sampleAnswer: Outdoor learning is fun and children can see real things. They get fresh air and exercise. But it depends on the weather. Classroom learning is organised and quiet. Children can focus better. But it can be boring for children to sit all day.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 3 - Compare two pictures

Which way of learning is better for children, in your opinion? Why?
questions.sampleAnswer: I prefer a mix of both for children. Outdoor learning is good for science and nature. Classroom learning is good for reading and writing. Children need both to learn well and stay interested.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 4 - Discuss an abstract topic

Tell me about a time when you faced a problem you could not solve.
questions.sampleAnswer:
Last year, I had a problem with my computer. It stopped working and I lost my important files. I tried many times to fix it but I could not. I felt very worried and stressed.
I asked my friend who is good with computers to help me. He looked at my computer and fixed the problem. He also helped me get my files back. I was very grateful for his help.
Yes, I think it is okay to ask for help. Nobody can do everything alone. When we ask for help, we can solve problems faster. Asking for help is not a weakness. It shows that we are smart enough to know our limits.
